contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty. Compatible with CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, and RED-0001. The finding correctly identifies that the rationality of S_6 irreps (classical Specht-module fact) guarantees only that the finite-monodromy direct image π_*Q_Y of the S_6-cover decomposes into Tate local systems; it does NOT force the full configuration-space local system (which includes H^1(C) coefficients from the curve family) to be Tate. Totaro's theorem (1996) shows configuration-space cohomology is built from H^*(C), and for a genus-6 tetragonal family the H^1(C) weight-1 variation is not a sum of Tate objects. Distinct from FND-0020 (mixed weights of R^1π_*Q for punctured curves), FND-0037 (non-split extension in forgetful Leray), and FND-0046–FND-0052 (geometric properties of the CE evaluation-failure locus). No merge target. Promote from candidate to corroborated on independent verification of: (1) all S_n irreps rational, (2) configuration-space cohomology depends on H^*(fiber), (3) H^1 of a curve family is a non-Tate weight-1 VHS. Evidence class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source.

scope.construction: S_6-cover of relative configuration/linear-system over tetragonal family

source_records.verification: All irreducible representations of S_n are defined over Q (Specht modules); classical fact confirmed by multiple sources.

Totaro (Topology 35, 1996) Theorem 4: rational cohomology of F(X,n) is determined by H^*(X). For a curve family, configuration-space cohomology carries the H^1(C) variation, which is a weight-1 non-Tate local system.
Casnati-Ekedahl structure theorem for degree-4 covers of P^1; the tetragonal family carries a weight-1 VHS on H^1(C).
